name: Courier Run
idea: One unbroken cobalt route writes C-N-X on a 45/90-degree street grid, leaving from a mint pickup dot and ending where a mint stroke crosses its last leg to mark the drop-off: X marks the spot.
why: The whole name is a single delivery run with a visible start and finish, and the X is literally the delivery point, so the logo is a one-sentence story people can retell.
risks: Continuous-line wordmarks are a familiar genre, and the octagonal C and rounded N hairpins can read as a cable or neon tube until the animation shows the route; the small CX monogram is less distinctive than the full wordmark.
